stem:
The diagram shows Meher's quadrilateral $ABCD$ with right-angle marks at $A$, $B$, and $D$, and with the remaining interior angle at $C$ labelled $x$.

Which claim about $x$ is correct?

options.text: $x$ must be $90^\circ$, because the four interior angles of a quadrilateral sum to $360^\circ$.
$x$ is only an interior-angle label, so the quadrilateral sum does not constrain it.
Drawing the four sides is what forces $x=90^\circ$, rather than the $360^\circ$ angle sum.
$x$ can be any size, because the diagram prints three right-angle marks.

teacher.key_rationale: Interior angles of a quadrilateral sum to 360°, so three right angles force the fourth to 90°. Treating x as a free label swaps the idea. Saying the drawn sides create the measure reverses the relation. Ignoring the sum because three marks are printed is a surface grab.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote grid-quadrilateral source into ABCD with three right-angle marks and x; stem refers to the diagram.
